'''Cepheids''' are stars whose [[luminosity|luminosities]] vary periodically over time.

== Properties ==

=== $T \propto L$ ===

First demonstrated by Leavitt and Shapley in the 1920s, the pulsating [[period]] of a cepheid is generally proportional to its [[luminosity]].<ref>{{#cite:Q2580}}</ref>

== Significance ==

As $T \propto L$, the [[luminosity]] ($L$) of a Cepheid can be estimated by observing its pulsating [[period]]. Hence, by additionally measuring its [[apparent brightness]] ($F_\mathrm{obs}$) as observed from earth and using the formula

{{#content:Q2586}}

its distance to earth $d$ can be estimated.

Using this technique, [[Person:Edwin Hubble|Edwin Hubble]] was able to estimate the distance to [[Andromeda]] from earth to be about $9 \cdot 10^{5} \mathrm{ly}$ baed on observations made via the $2.50 \mathrm{m}$ [[Mount Wilson telescope]], providing a hint to the vastness of the [[Universe]] to humanity.

<ref>{{#cite:Q2580}}</ref>

<blockquote>
The modern accepted distance from earth to Andromeda is about $2\cdot 10^{6}\mathrm{ly}$.<ref>{{#cite:Q2580}}</ref>
</blockquote>
